data.note:
Reflection: I was wrong — true MoA Eg5 inhibitors, I called Microtubule stabilizers (p=0.50).

What misled me: strong tubulin hyperintensity already at 0.3-1 uM (tub_mean z=21-26, rho=+1.0) with rising mitotic fraction, plus microscopist language of "dense filamentous signal" / "stabilized microtubules". I treated interphase brightening as stabilization bundles.

What I discounted: the atlas was consistently telling me Eg5 — 7/10 AZ-C neighbours at 1uM (e6), 7/10 at 0.3uM (e14), 7/10 combined 4-dose (e24). I rationalized this as cosine confound and kept stabilizers on top, only lowering to 0.50 on revision.

In hindsight compact bright tubulin masses in rounded mitotics with condensed DNA are exactly what monopolar Eg5 arrest looks like at this resolution — both microscopist reports explicitly said Eg5/Aurora cannot be excluded without resolved spindle polarity. Severe cell loss at 10uM (28 cells) made the high-dose profile saturated and unreliable.

Literature: Eg5 inhibition by small molecules produces monopolar spindles / loss of bipolarity with mitotic arrest (Mayer et al., Science 1999, PMID:10542155); Eg5 inhibitor K858 induces mitotic arrest and cell death (Nakai et al., Cancer Res 2009, PMID:19351824). This matches the rounded condensed-DNA + bright compact tubulin phenotype here.

Lesson: when low-dose atlas repeatedly returns same MoA (AZ-C Eg5) and visuals cannot resolve monopolar vs bundles, do not overrule atlas on intensity magnitude alone; need spindle-polarity imaging / tubulin polymerization assay as I listed for next lab step.

reflection.text:
We correctly recognized a potent antimitotic phenotype: frac_mitotic_like z=+159 at 10uM with rho=+1.00 across 0.3-10uM, falling cell counts and lower density, which correctly narrowed the field to mitotic MOAs and kept Eg5 in the hypothesis set. That arrest with monopolar spindle failure is the classic Eg5 phenotype (PMID 10542155), and Eg5 inhibition is known to cause prolonged mitotic arrest and cell death (PMID 19351824).

We were misled by tubulin intensity and texture: tub_mean z=+21 to +29 from 0.3-3uM with rho=+1.00 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+203 at 10uM was read as direct stabilization and used to raise Microtubule stabilizers to 0.68. In fact condensed monopolar spindles in Eg5 arrest also raise mean and contrast tubulin signal as mitotic fraction rises, so the tubulin trend was secondary to arrest, not proof of bundles.

The decisive miss was weighting and acquisition: we discounted three independent atlas calls of Eg5 7/10 in e6, e14 and e24 in favor of one e7 visual call of stabilizer alone, and we stopped at 4 wells over 0.3-10uM without the discriminating 30uM well or spindle-polarity imaging. Morphology-aware profiling is needed to separate these overlapping mitotic profiles (PMID 24997502), and the review clue that tubulin is lost at 30uM directly contradicts retained stabilizer bundles.
what_was_right: Detected potent dose-dependent antimitotic arrest with frac_mitotic_like z=+159 at 10uM and rho=+1.00 across 0.3-10uM plus cell loss, correctly narrowing to mitotic MOAs
Retained Eg5 inhibitors from early microscopist candidates and repeated atlas 7/10 calls in e6, e14, e24
Correctly rejected microtubule destabilizers and cholesterol-lowering because tub_mean and tub texture increased rather than decreased
what_was_wrong: Interpreted increased tub_mean, tub_glcm_contrast and rho=+1.00 as direct stabilization when Eg5 monopolar spindle condensation also raises these features with mitotic fraction
Over-weighted single e7 visual call of Microtubule stabilizers and early tub hyperintensity while discounting three repeated Eg5 7/10 atlas comparisons
Failed to acquire the discriminating 30uM well and high-resolution spindle-polarity images, missing that tubulin loss at high dose refutes the stabilizer-bundle model

citations.claim: Small-molecule Eg5 inhibition blocks spindle bipolarity producing monopolar spindles and mitotic arrest.
The Eg5 inhibitor K858 blocks mitotic kinesin Eg5 function and induces mitotic arrest and cell death.
Computational analysis of image-based profiles can distinguish drug mechanisms.

reflection.next_experiment: High-resolution alpha-tubulin plus pericentrin/centrosome immunofluorescence to score monopolar rosettes versus stabilized bundles, paired with an Eg5 ATPase assay versus an in vitro tubulin polymerization assay.
